prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Thrips in my plant room😬.

Any suggestions on eradicating them. Yesterday, I began spraying with a solution (70% alcohol / 29% water / 1% peppermint oil). I plan to spray all leaves every week. I have read that this will help control Thrips but not eradicate them. Any advice from people that have overcome thrips?

I have over 80 plants in my plant room and need to aggressively kill this invader. Some of my orchids are over 25 yrs old.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Thrips.** The pale yellow-white flecks are their feeding scars, and the tiny black dots along the midrib are their droppings.

**Stop the 70% alcohol spray.** Used weekly on all leaves, it can burn foliage, especially on your old orchids. It also can't reach thrips eggs inside the leaves or pupae in the soil, so the infestation keeps coming back.

1. **Spray spinosad.** Buy Captain Jack's Deadbug Brew concentrate (about $13). Mix about 4 tablespoons per gallon of water, or as the label directs. Spray leaf tops, undersides, stems and the soil surface until wet. Work in the evening, out of direct sun.
   - **Batches:** Do about 20 plants a day so each session stays under 15 minutes.
   - **Schedule:** Repeat every 7 days for 4 rounds to cover the whole life cycle.
2. **Hang blue sticky traps.** A pack of about 20 costs around $8. Put one at leaf level among each group of plants, with extra traps near the worst-hit ones.
3. **Count weekly.** Check the traps every week for about 5 minutes and note the number caught. Falling counts mean the spinosad is working. Replace traps when they fill up.
